basics.name: Mechanisms in Modern Engineering Design: A Handbook for Engineers, Designers and Inventors (Ivan I. Artobolevsky)
basics.url: No official publisher page (the Soviet publisher Mir no longer exists). Best bibliographic records: DMG-Lib series record https://www.dmg-lib.org/dmglib/handler?docum=3977009 (full text not available there) and DMG-Lib author page https://www.dmg-lib.org/dmglib/main/biogrViewer_content.jsp?id=183004&skipSearchBar=1 (lists the English, Russian and French editions). Scans of the English edition are on the Internet Archive as community uploads, e.g. https://archive.org/details/ArtobolevskyMechanismsInModernEngineeringDesignVol1, with no rights statement (see license)
basics.cost: Paid in print: out of print, second-hand sets and single volumes sell through used-book dealers (AbeBooks, eBay; prices vary widely and were not checked) [uncertain]. Unofficial scans can be read free online (see license)
basics.license: All rights reserved (copyrighted Soviet-era work, translated by Nicholas Weinstein and published by Mir, Moscow). No open licence exists. The Internet Archive copies are uploads by private users: the 2017 set has no rights field, and a 2021 upload of volumes 3 and 4 is tagged with a Public Domain Mark by the uploader, which is not backed by any evidence and should not be relied on [uncertain]. What this means for the encyclopedia: cite it and link to library/catalogue records, but do not copy its drawings or text
basics.language: Russian original; English translation (Mir, 5 volumes in 7 books); French translation 'Les mecanismes dans la technique moderne' (Mir, 1975-1978)
basics.year: Predecessor: 'Mechanisms' (Russian, 4 volumes, USSR Academy of Sciences, 1947-1952, about 4,000 mechanisms). Russian 'Mekhanizmy v sovremennoi tekhnike' 1st edition 1970-1976 (5 volumes), 2nd revised edition in 7 volumes 1979-1981 (Nauka, 3,248 pages). English translation 1975-1980 (Vol. 1 1975, Vol. 2 1976, Vols. 3-4 1977, Vol. 5 1979/1980), reprinted 1979. No later edition
basics.access_barrier: Paywall / out of print for legitimate copies (buy second-hand or borrow from a library). DMG-Lib holds catalogue records only (full text not available)
basics.image_license: All rights reserved, same as the text. The line drawings are copyrighted and cannot be reused. A 2024 research dataset (Ghezelbash, arXiv 2409.03763) scraped 4,142 of its 2D sketches; that does not make them free to reuse
basics.authority_level: academic / professional reference: compiled by Academician I. I. Artobolevsky (USSR Academy of Sciences, a founder and the first President of IFToMM, the International Federation for the Promotion of Mechanism and Machine Science). Not peer-reviewed in the modern sense, but the standard large mechanism catalogue of the 20th century

coverage.covers: Thousands of numbered mechanisms, each drawn and briefly described, across the whole of mechanical engineering. Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 (parts 1 and 2): lever mechanisms (linkages built from lower pairs), 2,288 mechanisms, starting with sections on the kinematic pairs themselves (Nos 1-54) and movable joints (Nos 55-119), then simple lever mechanisms (clamping, braking, stop/detent/locking, indexing, clutch, governor, safety, adjustment ...) and linkwork (four-bar to multi-link, parallel cranks, straight-line guides, dwell mechanisms, pantographs). Vol. 3: gear mechanisms (numbering continues from No. 2289). Vol. 4: cam, friction and flexible-link (belt, chain, cable) mechanisms. Vol. 5 part 1: hydraulic and pneumatic mechanisms; Vol. 5 part 2: electric mechanisms (sections 33-36: simple, lever-type, toothed and complex electric mechanisms). Many entries are whole devices from old machines, instruments and patents
coverage.organisation: Two-level system. First by construction (what the mechanism is made of: lever, gear, cam, friction, flexible-link, hydraulic, pneumatic, electric), which decides the volume and section; then, inside each section, by function (what it does: e.g. 'Gripping, Clamping and Expanding', 'Stop, Detent and Locking', 'Indexing', 'Clutch and Coupling', 'Dwell', 'Safety'). Mechanisms are numbered continuously through all volumes. Two tables at the front of Vol. 1 (Table 1: classification by structural features; Table 2: classification by functional features) cross-link the two schemes. For a beginner the functional sub-groups are the useful handle ('I need something that locks'), but you must already know which construction family to look in, the same function is spread over many volumes, and readers complain that the order inside a group is hard to follow
coverage.scope_match: high for mechanism TYPES: it is almost entirely clever mechanisms, with whole functional groups for locking, detents, indexing, clutches, safety devices, clamping and adjustment, plus full volumes on gear trains and on electric (electromagnet, solenoid, relay) mechanisms. Lower for makers: it is 1970s Soviet industrial practice with no 3D printing, snap fits, compliant joints or adhesives, and much of it is whole devices rather than single connectors
coverage.taxonomy_used: Artobolevsky's structural-functional classification (building on the Assur-Artobolevsky structural theory of mechanisms). Top level by construction type, 5 volumes / about 36 numbered sections in the English edition: Vol. 1 sections 1-3 are 'Elements of Mechanisms' (kinematic pairs and movable joints), 'Simple Lever Mechanisms' and 'Linkwork'; Vol. 2 carries on with further lever-mechanism families (in the Russian 2nd edition these are slotted-link, crank-slider, lever-cam, lever-gear, lever-ratchet, lever-wedge, screw-lever and flexible/elastic-link mechanisms) [uncertain]; Vol. 3 starts at Section 13 'Simple Gear Mechanisms'; Vol. 5 part 2 is Sections 33-36. Second level: about 30 recurring functional groups (from the Vol. 1 contents): lever mechanisms; gripping, clamping and expanding; balance; brake; stop, detent and locking; switching, engaging and disengaging; indexing; sorting and feeding; governor; clutch and coupling; measuring and testing devices; hammer, press and die; key; materials handling; safety; link-length adjustment; mathematical operations; contacting lever; general-purpose four-, five-, six- and multi-link; parallel-crank; crossed-crank; guiding mechanisms and inversors; dwell; curve-generating; film-camera claw; pantograph; other functional devices. Each functional group has a short letter index (e.g. SD for stop, detent and locking) [uncertain]
coverage.example_types: stop, detent and locking mechanisms (Nos 258-334); indexing mechanisms (Nos 362-405); switching, engaging and disengaging mechanisms; clutch and coupling mechanisms; safety mechanisms; gripping, clamping and expanding mechanisms (e.g. toggle clamps) (Nos 163-245); brake mechanisms; link-length adjustment mechanisms; governor mechanisms (centrifugal); dwell mechanisms; straight-line guiding mechanisms and inversors (e.g. Peaucellier); pantographs; parallel-crank mechanisms; film-camera claw (intermittent pull-down) mechanisms; kinematic pairs and movable joints drawn pictorially (Nos 1-119); lever-ratchet mechanisms [uncertain]; gear trains incl. planetary and differential gears (Vol. 3) [uncertain for the exact section names]; cam, friction-drive and belt/chain/cable (flexible-link) mechanisms (Vol. 4); electromagnet- and solenoid-driven electric mechanisms (Vol. 5 part 2) [uncertain for the exact types]
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering: machine tools, instruments, engines, vehicles, automation (industrial practice of the 1940s-1970s). Not aimed at 3D printing or hobby making
coverage.item_count: Continuous numbering across all 7 books. Vols 1-2: 2,288 lever mechanisms (Vol. 1 alone: Nos 1-912). Vol. 3 starts at No. 2289. A reader quotes No. 4737 from Vol. 5, so the English edition has at least about 4,700 mechanisms, probably more [uncertain]. The 'about 4,000' figure belongs to the 1947-1952 Russian predecessor. The printed set runs to roughly 3,250 pages (Russian 2nd edition: 3,248 pages)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: partly, through safety mechanisms and clutch/coupling groups (e.g. overload-release devices) [uncertain for specific slip-clutch entries]; self-locking: yes (stop, detent and locking group; toggle and wedge clamps; screw mechanisms); hand-release only: partly (locking and clamping devices released by a lever or key) [uncertain]; one-way/ratchet: yes (lever-ratchet mechanisms, indexing with pawls) [uncertain for the Vol. 2 section title]; indexing/detent: yes (dedicated 'Indexing' and 'Stop, Detent and Locking' groups); over-centre: yes, as toggle clamps and dead-centre locking within the clamping and locking groups [uncertain]; compliant: only partly (mechanisms with elastic links, i.e. springs, are a structural family) [uncertain]; print-in-place: no; gear trains/gearboxes: yes, a whole volume (Vol. 3); powered connectors: yes, Vol. 5 (hydraulic, pneumatic and electric mechanisms, including electromagnet- and solenoid-operated devices) [uncertain for specific latch examples]; adhesive types: no
coverage.entry_structure: Mechanism number, group heading, short name, a simple line drawing (schematic or isometric, with lettered links), and a plain-text description of how it moves; some entries add formulas (relationships between link lengths, displacements and velocities). Inventor names are given only when well known. No sources are cited per entry, no dimensions for building, no photos
coverage.audience_level: professional (engineers, designers, technicians) and inventors; the author says he avoided specialist jargon so that people without engineering training can follow it

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: low to medium. The author deliberately used simple drawings and plain descriptions, and the functional groups are intuitive. But the drawings are dense 1970s schematics, the descriptions are terse and full of reference letters, there are thousands of entries with little explanation of why you would choose one, and forum readers find the order 'no obvious order' and the explanations hard to follow
usefulness.has_images: yes. Every mechanism has a line drawing (schematic or isometric). Quality is mixed: clear but small and old-fashioned, and scans online vary in quality
usefulness.has_animations: no (print book). Some of its mechanisms have been animated by others (e.g. Nguyen Duc Thang's videos), but not as a set
usefulness.gaps: No maker methods (3D printing, laser cutting), no snap fits, living hinges, compliant or print-in-place joints, no adhesives; no dimensions, tolerances or materials; no selection guidance or comparison between alternatives; out of print, copyrighted and hard to get legally; old-fashioned examples; the functional index is split across volumes; no per-entry URLs
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: low. There are no stable legitimate per-mechanism web pages. The best you can do is cite 'Artobolevsky, Vol. X, No. NNNN' in text, and link to a catalogue record such as https://www.dmg-lib.org/dmglib/handler?docum=3977009. Linking to the unlicensed scans on the Internet Archive is not recommended
usefulness.reusable_data: Not reusable as a dataset from the publisher. The classification scheme itself (the list of structural families and functional group names) is an idea, not protected expression, and can be adapted with attribution. A 2024 research dataset ('A Dataset for Mechanical Mechanisms', about 9,000 images, 4,142 of them 2D sketches taken from Artobolevsky Vols 1-4) is on GitHub (farghea/database_for_mechanical_mechanism) with images on Google Drive. The arXiv paper is CC0, but the scraped images keep their original copyright
usefulness.maintained: No. Closed historical work (last Russian edition 1979-1981; English 1975-1980). The author died in 1977 and Mir Publishers no longer exists. It lives on through used copies, libraries and unofficial scans
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) The two-axis index: classify each entry both by what it is made of (construction family) and by what it does (function), and link the two in a cross-reference table. This maps well onto a flow chart ('what do you need it to do?' then 'which kind of parts can you make?'). (2) Functional group names written as plain needs: 'Stop, Detent and Locking', 'Gripping, Clamping and Expanding', 'Switching, Engaging and Disengaging', 'Link-Length Adjustment', 'Safety'. (3) Start the catalogue with the basic joints (kinematic pairs and movable joints) drawn pictorially rather than as symbols. (4) Continuous numbering so every entry has a short, citable ID. (5) One simple drawing per entry plus a short 'how it moves' paragraph
usefulness.design_rules_given: Few. Some entries give analytical relationships (link-length ratios, displacement and velocity formulas) for kinematics, mainly for guiding and dwell mechanisms. No clearances, fits, strengths, materials or torque values [uncertain]
usefulness.file_formats: Printed book. Unofficial scans exist online as PDF/DjVu; no CAD, STL or data files
usefulness.terminology_value: medium. Good for systematic English names of mechanism families and functional groups (via the translator's standard terms), and for Russian-English equivalents through the parallel editions. Some terms are Soviet-translation style (e.g. 'linkwork', 'flexible-link mechanisms', 'inversors') and differ from modern Western or maker usage
usefulness.decision_support: Partial. The functional classification (Table 2) lets a designer look up mechanisms by the job they must do, and Table 1 by structure. There is no flow chart, filter or comparison of pros and cons
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Revised and enlarged successor of Artobolevsky's own 'Mechanisms' (1947-1952), compiled from textbooks, journals and patents (sources not listed). Its theory rests on the Assur-Artobolevsky structural classification and on Reuleaux's kinematic pairs. Overlaps heavily with Jones' 'Ingenious Mechanisms for Designers and Inventors', Sclater's 'Mechanisms and Mechanical Devices Sourcebook', Hiscox's '1800 Mechanical Movements' and '507 Mechanical Movements' for the classic items. Its drawings feed the 2024 'Dataset for Mechanical Mechanisms' (together with DMG-Lib videos and Nguyen Duc Thang's animations). DMG-Lib catalogues all its editions (English, Russian, French)
